elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “Customer, its affiliates.”

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes Customer's “contractors acting on Customer's behalf.”
The clause does not state that any paid-up licence is perpetual and instead permits revocation upon expiration or termination. It is not demonstrably established that paid-up licences cannot arise.
The licence remains revocable upon expiration or termination, and the retained language states that the licence “shall be revoked.” No irrevocability protection is provided for paid-up licences.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: The licence is revocable upon any expiration or termination of the Agreement in accordance with paragraph 4; the operative language does not limit termination to material breach. Paragraph 4 is not provided as evidence of such a limitation.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: No uncured-breach requirement or cure period appears in the rendered language. Subscription licensing is not demonstrably inapplicable.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors without restriction to a particular type of succession transaction.
elements.evidence: Transfer is limited to successors arising through merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transactions and purchasers of all or substantially all relevant assets, rather than successors generally.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered upon Customer's written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are included automatically in the licence grant, without needing notice. This provides at least the coverage available under the written-notice fallback.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly transferable to a successor by merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction and to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback because affiliates receive immediate coverage and M&A-successor transfer is expressly permitted. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits perpetual and irrevocable treatment for paid-up licences, does not restrict subscription termination to uncured material breach, and limits successor transfer to specified M&A contexts. It is not minimal to the completed fallback because it also adds contractor coverage and revises revocation language without completing the preferred termination protections. The changes otherwise remain directed to licence scope and do not materially disturb unrelated commercial terms.
